highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should be aware of this release as it may soon power more advanced coding assistance features within their workflows.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.225: Gateway Spend Limits & Workspace Trust for Agents
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.225 adds clearer spend-limit warnings that now display the cap name, reset time, and your operator's message when you hit a usage ceiling — helpful for teams managing costs. It also introduces a workspace trust prompt for `claude agents` in untrusted directories, adding an important safety check before agents run in unfamiliar codebases.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.224: Self-Hosted Runners & Archive Plugin Source
highlights.summary: This release lets Team and Enterprise users turn their own machines or containers into Claude Code runners via `claude self-hosted-runner`, giving more control over where code executes. It also adds an `archive` plugin source so you can install plugins from a zip file over HTTPS without needing a git repository.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.222: Worktree Isolation & Hook Security Fixes
highlights.summary: This security-focused release fixes a bug where worktree-isolated sessions could run destructive git commands against the main checkout — isolation now properly covers both file edits and Bash commands. It also patches a vulnerability where PreToolUse auto-allow hooks could bypass tool restrictions in background agent tasks.

highlights.title: Claude Code Full Course – Autonomous Goals, MCP, and VS Code Setup
highlights.summary: This comprehensive YouTube course walks through setting up Claude Code in VS Code and covers advanced topics like MCP (Model Context Protocol) and autonomous goal-driven workflows. It's an excellent all-in-one resource for developers who want to move beyond basic usage and start building more powerful AI-assisted pipelines.

highlights.title: How To Use Claude Code To Build Anything (for Beginners)
highlights.summary: This beginner-friendly YouTube tutorial shows how to use Claude Code to build real projects from scratch, even with little coding experience. It covers the core workflow of prompting, reviewing changes, and iterating — making it a great starting point for anyone new to AI-assisted development.

highlights.title: Wallfacer – A Terminal Session Manager for Claude Code
highlights.summary: Wallfacer is a community-built terminal session manager designed to help developers juggle multiple Claude Code sessions more efficiently. If you regularly run parallel tasks or background agents, this tool could streamline how you organize and switch between them.

highlights.title: Agent Skills for Team Coding Standards in Claude Code
highlights.summary: This GitHub project provides reusable agent skills that automatically enforce team coding standards inside Claude Code and Codex, reducing the need to manually remind the AI about style rules or conventions. Teams can share these skills across members to ensure consistent, policy-compliant code generation.

tips_of_the_day: Before running Claude Code agents in any new directory, check whether VS Code trusts that workspace — untrusted directories can now trigger a safety prompt, so setting trust explicitly prevents unexpected interruptions in your workflow.

If your team keeps hitting usage limits mid-session, ask your administrator to configure a gateway spend limit with a clear operator message; the updated warning (v2.1.225+) will tell you exactly when the cap resets so you can plan your coding sessions accordingly.

Use shared agent skill files (like those in the adlc-team-skills project) to codify your team's coding conventions once and have Claude Code apply them automatically — this saves time vs. repeating style instructions in every prompt.
